issues.title: `bro act wait --merge` reports 'already merged' as a verdict, not as a failure
issues.description:
When auto-merge lands the PR first, the act watcher finds the PR already MERGED. Today that
path is undefined for the caller: the watcher should exit 0 with a verdict that says 'already
merged by <actor>', so the formula's merge step can close on it without the agent inventing a
result. Today the agent has to read the PR and write the verdict by hand — which is exactly how
a merge step ends up closed on a claim.

issues.title: brouter.models keys — schema validator propertyNames support for key validation
issues.description:
PR #735 (bro-n1p0s) follow-up from CodeRabbit on the brouter config schema.

Finding: the brouter schema applies `js.map` to `models`, and `js.map`
constrains only the values — so a key like `" "` passes schema
validation. `parseBrouter` then drops that key at load time with a
`console.error` warning. The validation surfaces (`bro doctor`,
`--strict`, the policy gate) report the config as valid, so the dropped
route is only visible in the load-time warning.

Why it is not fixed inline: the schema validator
(packages/core/src/schema-validator.ts) does not support `propertyNames`
today, so rejecting a key needs validator support first. Changing
`js.map` globally would change every section that uses it
(`connectorsSection`, `providersSection`, the fleet maps, …), so the
brouter schema cannot express the constraint alone.

Suggested scope:
1. Add `propertyNames` support to the schema validator (draft-07
   keyword) — a core validator feature, its own change with tests.
2. Use it in `brouterSection.jsonSchema` to reject keys that trim to
   an empty string.
3. Decide the same question for the other key maps — `providers` and
   `connectors` trim/drop empty keys at parse time the same way, so the
   gap is repo-wide, not brouter-specific.

Related: bro-xgjha (brouter.ts code-health tail).

issues.title: minimax lane: harden model-centric routing (mandatory model-pin)
issues.description:
Standing queue-keeper for the lane configured under fleet.routing's minimax CLASS (operator config layer). Continuation of the merged model-centric registry (#735) and of drill 2026-10-30-093836-78f5c92-minimax-model-mismatch (root cause: loop.ts lanePicks model-fallback leak; prevention: backlog item).

Scope (provider-agnostic core mechanics — valid for ANY operator's lane config):
1. Make the inline model-pin in fleet.routing.<class>.chain mandatory for every routed class: validation rejects a chain entry with provider but no model UNLESS the provider entry itself carries a model (auto-default from providers.<name>.model at declaration).
2. Keep the #813 invariant (profileModelFor: a profile model may only be inherited by its own provider) covered by tests so a future pin-less config cannot leak a lane default again.
3. Tests red-before/green-after: chain without model AND without provider model = validation failure; provider-default resolution = green. cs delta clean.

Queue mechanics: beads for this lane must carry the class label defined by the operator's routing config (personal layer — never hardcoded here). When this bead closes, the operator tops up the queue.

issues.title: diagnostics: reconstruct Devin last rate-limit lock (sessions.db + session_locks/procs + serve-turns)
issues.description:
## Context (2026-11-07 retro)
Diagnosing 'what drove Devin into rate limit' required manual forensics: scanning ~/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db message_nodes tail for 'Reached free model rate limit' (bounded row_id DESC), finding sessions active at lock time, inventorying live devin processes (devin -r, devin acp*), mapping session_locks/*.lock→pid/cwd, and correlating .git/bro/serve-turns.jsonl + bro fleet agents status.

## Problem
There is no single bro command to answer: when was the last Devin lock, which session hit it, what reset window was quoted, and which devin consumers/processes were active in parallel.

## Proposed action
Add a read-only diagnostic (e.g. 'bro fleet devin diagnose --last-lock' or 'bro self diagnose devin-rate-limit') that reports:
- last rate-limit hit(s) from devin sessions.db (best-effort, bounded scan, read-only)
- session id/model/dir/title, trace id, reset mark, timestamp
- sessions active around lock time
- live devin processes + lock owners (pid, cmd, cwd, fleet mapping when available)
- recent devin-acp/serve conductor activity summary
Fail-open when sessions.db/proc/serve logs are unavailable; never mutate state.

issues.title: the command base — bro and brouter as two instances of one bootstrap
issues.description:
Child of bro-olfvd.

The dispatch lived inside bro's CLI package, so brouter had to grow its own
(a second hand-written switch — exactly the duplication the parser move just
removed). The base is shared: a plugin registry, the group dispatch, the help
tables, the argv rules.

New package @broject/command — a bootstrap for ANY cli, zero dependencies.
It knows nothing about bro, beads, the bus or the fleet: the tree is the
caller's. A command is a mini-CLI (it holds commands and plugins), and the
bin decides what is executable — any command can become its own binary.
Four modules: plugin (the definition + definePlugin), command (defineCommand /
runCommand / the member table / usage text), registry (external registration,
reserved and taken names), exits (the 0/1/2 codes and the usage writer).

Two instances of one base: bro = the base + bro's plugin set + bro's doc
layer (the doc verbs stay bro's fallback resolver). brouter = the base +
brouter's plugin set. `bro router` is a thin wrapper: it MOUNTS brouter's
plugins with bro's policy (the live serve state, the configured client
settings path) — a mount, not a second switch. No behavior change for bro:
the tables move verbatim; the registry tests and the CLI suite guard it.

citty is the parser LAYER (a later step, brouter first — bro's ~150 commands
migrate under the command-docs/contract gates). opentui is the REPL's renderer
(M6), and the repo's own acp-view layer is the reference.

Scope: packages/command (new), bro's index.ts/plugins.ts rewired, brouter's
commands as plugins. Out of scope: the citty swap, the REPL, the
served-catalog whitelist (M2), the interactive setter (M3).

issues.title: packages/cli: **WARNING:** Missing rollback case for claimed step with no previous assignee `rollbackSpawnWrite` handles `claimed && …
issues.description:
**WARNING:** Missing rollback case for claimed step with no previous assignee

`rollbackSpawnWrite` handles `claimed && previousAssignee !== undefined` (restore previous assignee) and `!claimed` (fresh claim reopen), but drops the `claimed && previousAssignee === undefined` case. The old code did a best-effort `store.reopen(spec.molStep)` here (pre-refactor agent-connectors.ts). Without it, a failed spawn after `rebindStep` on a step that had no assignee leaves an orphaned `in_progress` claim, blocking all future respawns of that step — `guardClaim` refuses with "claimed by … — rebind only takes our own claim".

Add an `else` branch for `claimed && previousAssignee === undefined` that reopens the claim when the step still carries this spawn's assignee, mirroring the compare-and-set guard used in the other branches.

issues.title: acp guard: a completion must remove its OWN session's charge
issues.description:
The guard's done() decrements the scope's (and the peer's) pending count by one, whoever calls it. Two holes follow:

1. A session that completes AFTER the churn window rolled decrements a NEWER session's charge — the window resets pending to 0 and starts counting the new session's opens, so the old completion takes the new session's charge and the churn is under-counted.
2. A retained session's later prompts decrement again (fixed in this PR by resolving a session's open once), but the underlying shape is the same: the counter has no idea WHICH open a completion belongs to.

The fix is a per-open token: open() hands back a handle (the scope, the peer, and the window generation the open was counted in), and done(handle) removes exactly that charge — and only if the window it was counted in is still the current one. The tally needs a generation counter that is bumped when the window resets.

issues.title: hooks telemetry: journal argv+exitCode, separate verdict from failed, tag one-shot vs long-runner in perf records
issues.description:
From drill 7c1a9d (hook cmd anomaly, parent 4b7e19):

journalCommand (packages/cli/src/index.ts:176) records only argv[0] at
process exit — so perf `ms` = WHOLE PROCESS LIFETIME (acp-worker p50 925s,
loop max 8.9h — by construction >10s) and the aggregate mean (28.9s) is a
mixture artifact, not latency. Also act.ts:417 exit-1 (gate red) is
journaled as failed:true — 49 of 79 "failures" are semantic verdicts.

Fix:
1. journal argv (full or subcommand+arity) + numeric exitCode.
2. Split verdict (exit 1 from gate/act) from failed (crash/timeout).
3. Tag rows kind: one-shot|long-runner (acp-worker/loop/daemon excluded
   from latency aggregates); report per-command p95.

Acceptance: drill-style aggregate reports real hook latency (p50/p95 per
event) without process-lifetime pollution; failed count = true failures
only; review rows distinguishable by subcommand.

Evidence: drill 7c1a9d §1-2 (drop-35 → mean 1177ms < p95; 49/79
verdicts; 41 acp-worker rows all >10s by construction).

Worth one sentence on what an `openai-compat` entry with no `apiKeyEnv` does when the judge consumes it — fail at startup, or proceed unauthenticated — so implementers don't have to guess between the two existing precedents.

issues.title: a merge step whose formula is unreadable closes without a verdict
issues.description:
Found on PR #960 (bro-4cxnd): the verifier classifies a step as the merge step from two signals — the poured issue's type (merge-step) and the molecule's formula (bd formula show). When a merge step was flattened to task AND its formula can no longer be read, the classification is unavailable and the step closes as a plain step: a claim, not a verdict.

The root cause is closed: bro convoy pour now reads types.custom back and refuses to pour when merge-step cannot be registered, so in bro's own flow the merge step never flattens. The formula fallback covers a molecule poured by plain bd mol pour.

The residual needs a molecule whose formula was removed from bd after the pour. Refusing there would also refuse every hand-made molecule's steps (bd mol distill pours task steps), so the narrow fix is a second signal the declaration survives: e.g. the formula's own file in the repo's formulas/ dir, read when bd's registry lost it.

Pointer: PR #960, the CodeRabbit finding on packages/cli/src/commands/convoy.ts (isMergeStep).

The compatibility list maps `judge.baseUrl`/`judge.model`/`judge.apiKeyEnv` → anonymous `systemone` entry and `judge.llm` → anonymous `openai-compat` entry, but the only existing consumer of those fields is the **chain** (packages/judge/src/chain.ts:205-217), where `judge.fallback` names a *connector* resolved via the connector registry. The synthesis section should pin the legacy behavior: e.g. `judge.fallback: 'llm-judge'` resolves to the synthesized `openai-compat` entry (and `'systemone'` to the synthesized `systemone` entry), so a legacy config's escalation semantics survive the migration release.

issues.title: loop run record on shared live pid survives reap — stale 'running' row after worktree teardown
issues.description:
Repro: bead run finishes, --cleanup deletes its worktree, but loop/<bead>.json records pid=<shared loop supervisor>. reapLoopRuns() (packages/cli/src/commands/loop-state.ts:237) only checks pidAlive(pid,pidStart) — the supervisor pid stays alive serving other runs, so the finished run's record keeps rendering 'running' in bro watch forever (observed: bro-nwl5g silent 188m after merge+cleanup, pid 87262 shared with bro-1wdo1/bro-kkm75).

Root cause: liveness is keyed on the recorded pid alone; two runs on one supervisor are indistinguishable, and a completed run's residue inherits the sibling's liveness.

Fix direction: reap when the record's worktree path is gone (filesystem check), or record a per-run identifier (runId/pgid) instead of the supervisor pid so pidAlive is per-run. Dead-pid records already self-reap at next 'bro loop' start; shared-pid ones need the extra signal.

bro mesh — decentralized request network between bro rigs
issues.description:
Vision: a decentralized network of bro projects ('bro mesh'). Each rig is sovereign; requests between rigs ride the existing beads bus — refs/dolt/data on each repo's git remote.

Core design: NO foreign writes. Requests live in the REQUESTER's beads store, addressed to a target rig (e.g. 'request → bro: <title>'), published via normal bd push. Peers subscribe read-only to each other's dolt refs (git fetch refs/dolt/data — public repos publish their store for free). The addressed rig sees inbound requests on its next pull, claims one, status (accepted/done) flows back through its own remote. Publish-subscribe over git — wasteland's sovereign-fork model without requiring a DoltHub commons.

Layers:
1. Rig identity/registry — .bro-rig.json or bead-addressed identity (pattern: gastown .town.json); how rigs name each other (beads://<org>/<repo>/<id> URI exists upstream).
2. Request envelope — bead type/label convention for cross-rig requests + response threading.
3. Peer subscription — 'bro peers add <git-remote>' → fetch foreign dolt ref, surface inbound requests in bd ready (hydration pattern exists: repos.primary/additional).
4. Wasteland bridge (optional, later) — public rigs post/claim via wl-commons wanted board; reputation lives there.

Relation to bro-5nnj (cross-repo request protocol): 5nnj phase 1-2 build the bilateral primitive (local request + external dep + wait watcher); mesh generalizes to N rigs. Do not design phase 1 in a way that assumes direct foreign-store writes — the mesh model forbids them.

herdr plugin: durable worktree<->agent-session ledger + classified reaper
issues.description: Durable worktree<->agent-session ledger + classified reaper + 'bro resume'. CONTEXT: 'dead' workspaces are mostly EXITED workers on live work. (1) LEDGER: every spawn path writes {worktree, agentKind, providerSessionId, command, model, beadId, spawnedAt, exitedAt, exitStatus, cause, promptLog} — native registry does this for loop workers; herdr plugin + manual spawns must write too. Dual storage: central .git/bro/ + worktree-local .bro/session. (2) REAPER classification: exited+open-PR=paused (resume candidate), no-PR+dirty=salvage/respawn, clean+no-PR+no-commits=corpse. workspace close safe always. (3) LABELS: render exited/interrupted/lost/stopped from cause+exitStatus, not lossy 'dead'. (4) 'bro resume <worktree|bead>' — BETTER than acpx auto-resume (acpx.sh/CLI#auto-resume): acpx keys sessions by (agentCommand,dir) so 'who was last' is unanswerable; ours keys by worktree with agentKind in the record => any-agent resume. Resume = re-arm the GATE (record carries beadId/DONE_CRITERIA), not just reconnect a conversation. issues.title: specs/bro-ribc.1.md: **WARNING:** "Unknown type drops the entry with a warning" conflicts with the adjacent no-silent-misconfig rule Rules 1…
issues.description:
**WARNING:** "Unknown type drops the entry with a warning" conflicts with the adjacent no-silent-misconfig rule

Rules 1 and 2 interact badly: an unknown `type` drops the entry (with a warning), but a consumer referencing that name must "error at use" — while a consumer referencing a *missing* name is "a startup error naming the missing key". So `provider: 'orca'` errors at startup when the entry is absent but only at use-time when the entry exists with a typoed `type` — the same user mistake (`'opena-compat'`) gets two different failure latencies and only the second one mentions the actual cause (the dropped entry), since the error at use can't name the missing key. Consider dropping the entry AND erroring at startup if any consumer reference resolves to a kind-invalid entry, or at least specifying what the use-time error says.

issues.title: brouter M1: the client layer — the served catalog rendered into a client's own model block (claude-code pilot)
issues.description:
Child of bro-olfvd.

The gateway serves the catalog (GET /v1/models), but the CLIENT filters it: Claude Code's discovery keeps only ids matching /(claude|anthropic)/i, so an honest <entry>/<model> id never reaches the picker (measured: 547 rows served, 89 survive the filter). Design: an abstract ClientAdapter in @broject/brouter — id, title, the settings key that carries the model block, how the block is rendered from the served catalog, how the settings merge (non-destructive), and the wiring (env) the client needs to reach the router. The claude-code adapter is the pilot: modelPicker {options, replaceBuiltInOptions} with a behavesAs per model family (the client borrows a model it knows, so context/effort/prompt profile are right).

Scope: packages/brouter (new package, a bin: brouter), the adapter interface + the claude-code pilot, the brouter CLI (models / clients / client <id> --write), the catalog reader (the live gateway's /v1/models), tests. bro serve client delegates to it — the filter fix lands in bro at once.

Out of scope: the served-catalog whitelist (M2), the interactive setter (M3), moving the gateway (M4), the acp client/ask (M5), the TUI (M6).

issues.title: the merge verdict reads references in the canonical GitHub shape only — the host's deep links and case rules are not read
issues.description:
Found on PR #960 (bro-4cxnd), CodeRabbit on packages/core/src/gh.ts and packages/convoy/src/verify.ts:

1. Deep links: the verifier recognizes the canonical /owner/repo/pull/N link and the bare #N form. A PR named only through a deep link (a /files suffix, a discussion fragment) names no PR — the claim is unverifiable and the merge step stays open. The caller has to retry with --pr N or a canonical link.

2. Case rules: two references that differ only in the owner's capitalization (GitHub is case-insensitive) are read as two repositories, and a case-only host difference fails the host check. Both can refuse a merged PR that should close the step.

The case rules are host-specific — a connector knows them, the core does not. Fix: the reference parser takes the host's rules from the connector (the way the verdict already takes its host), and the identity comparison asks the connector whether two spellings are the same object.

issues.title: packages/cli: <!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 --> **🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win** **The comment promis…
issues.description:
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**The comment promises a hydration retry that never runs.**

When the hydration text is empty, Line 401 clears `hydration` so that "the next turn deserves a retry". Nothing calls `hydrate()` again: `beforeAgentStart` only reads `hydration`. One failed `session-start` probe therefore leaves the whole session with no hydration. For example, the probe can hit the 45 s timeout, or the CLI can fail to resolve before `RESOLVE_RETRY_MS` expires.

issues.title: no occupancy signal for uncommitted work in a shared checkout — git mutations can step on a live session's WIP
issues.description:
Incident: auxiliary session ran 'git stash' + 'git pull' in the main checkout where the primary orchestrator (herdr pane w0:pW) had uncommitted WIP (agents.ts +168). Work survived via stash pop, but nothing told me the dirty tree was possibly-live — .work markers (bro/hooks/*.work) record armed sessions only by id, and a foreign session's uncommitted changes carry no ownership metadata.

The missing surface: before git-mutating a shared checkout, an agent needs one command answering 'who owns this dirty state?'. Options: (a) sessions that touch a repo stamp a checkout-level marker (.git/bro/hooks/<session>.work already exists — extend its record with the checkout path it owns + heartbeat), (b) 'bro work status'/'bro doctor' row listing live sessions whose cwd/marker resolves to this checkout, (c) a pre-mutation check in bro work enter/leave that warns 'dirty tree + live session marker → hands off'.

Heuristic that failed and needs codifying: file mtime is NOT ownership evidence — a paused live session's writes look identical to a crashed session's residue.

issues.title: conductor /v1/messages: decide + land thinking-field handling — budget_tokens to thought_level, or document the accepted no-op
issues.description:
specs/bro-bvipw.md feature matrix marks `thinking` / extended thinking ❌ '**decide**: map budget → thought_level pin, or emit thinking blocks?' — the decision was never made and no child owns it.

Today: MessagesRequest (serve-conductor.ts ~L515) has no `thinking` field; claude-code's `thinking:{type:'enabled',budget_tokens:N}` is tolerated silently as an unknown field, so an extended-thinking turn runs at whatever thought_level the model pin carries. The OpenAI plane already maps `reasoning.effort` → composite pin (effortModel, serve-conductor.ts ~L3100) — the anthropic plane has no equivalent.

Audit evidence (origin/main 60dbdf36): 'budget_tokens' appears nowhere outside specs/bro-bvipw.md; spec .1 explicitly descoped it ('No thinking ... work — ACP has no knobs') but the master matrix still carries the ❌.

Resolution paths (owner's call):
- map: `thinking.type==='enabled'` + budget_tokens → thought_level leaf on the pin (thresholds e.g. <4k→low, <16k→medium, else high — or always append the session's max when enabled); `thinking.type==='disabled'` → strip any effort leaf. Must not break the `<base>-<level>` pin resolution or the fast-lane shape test (thinking field must not flip fastShaped).
- document: flip the matrix row to ⚠️ accepted no-op with rationale (ACP thought_level is pin-driven; claude's budget is a hint the backend cannot honour per-token).

Either way the matrix row stops lying. Verify: hermetic test in serve-conductor.test.ts for whichever path lands.

issues.title: conductor dialect polish: OpenAI /v1/models row shape + unknown-model 404 (spec leftovers)
issues.description:
specs/bro-bvipw.md carries two wire-fidelity rows the shipped dialects only half meet (audit origin/main 60dbdf36). Both are "decide implement-vs-document" items — real codex exec works without them, so P3.

1. `GET /v1/models` OpenAI shape — spec: `{object:'list', data:[{id, object:'model', created, owned_by}]}` over the same catalog; the planned hermetic test ("/v1/models in OpenAI shape", serve-conductor-codex.test.ts) never landed — serve-conductor-openai.test.ts has no /v1/models case. Today ONE endpoint serves both planes: envelope `{object:'list', data, has_more, first_id, last_id}` (a hybrid — anthropic pagination fields + the OpenAI list marker) and rows are anthropic-shaped (`type:'model'`, `display_name`, `created_at`, `source`; no `object:'model'`, `created`, `owned_by`). An OpenAI client parsing rows strictly sees the wrong shape. Options: content-negotiate on Accept/path (bro-rjc93 already wants per-dialect base paths — coordinate), emit the OpenAI row fields additively (cheap, both shapes tolerate extras), or flip the spec row to "shared hybrid, documented".

2. Unknown model pin → 404 `not_found_error` — spec error table target; today `routeOf` deliberately rides an unmatched/unknown prefix on the default lane ("a model id the default's catalog cannot serve is that lane's own verdict") and no catalog-membership check exists, so a typo'd pin surfaces as the provider's own failure (529/500-class), not a 404. Retry semantics differ: claude-code retries 5xx/529, not 404 — a bad pin currently costs retry storms. Options: validate the resolved pin against the lane's catalog before acpTurn (catalog read is cached? check laneCatalog cost — a cold read spawns the agent, so this may need a session-config rejection path instead), map the acp "unknown model" error class to 404 in turnError, or document the deviation.

Verify: hermetic cases in serve-conductor.test.ts / serve-conductor-openai.test.ts for whichever resolution lands; update specs/bro-bvipw.md rows to match reality.

## Evidence (2026-11-07 retro)
At 2026-11-07T04:41:22Z Devin lock, 3 devin processes were alive sharing the account: pid 3049202 'devin -r' (cwd /home/pepl/projects/bro, started 2026-11-04), pid 3051633 'devin acp' (fleet devin:speckled-water), pid 3133355 'devin acp --model swe-2-high' (fleet devin:abalone-sawfish, many session_locks). The interactive 'devin -r' process is an unmanaged consumer not obviously represented in the quota picture the operator reasons about.

## Problem
Operators assume '1 herdr session + 1 subagent = 2 consumers', but unmanaged/interactive devin processes and serve-spawned work can consume the same account quota. Fleet/plane visibility and quota reasoning need to surface these consumers clearly.

## Proposed action
1. Ensure devin session plane/connector/fleet status surfaces all live devin CLI processes/sessions relevant to the account, including interactive REPL/resumed sessions where detectable.
2. In status/diagnostics, distinguish managed fleet workers vs discovered/external devin sessions and warn when unmanaged consumers are present during quota pressure.
3. Coordinate with bro-eqi2d (external-agent exclusion + quota ceiling across providers) so counting/admission use the same visibility.

issues.title: [bug] ensureFixerWorktree: absent first slug path returns before namespaced fallback is tried — existing checkout never reused
issues.description: Deferred from https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/pull/1036 thread PRRT_kwDOUamqtM620jAD (codeant-ai, Major/logic). In packages/rig/src/fixer-worktree.ts the candidate loop does 'return addFixerWorktree(...)' on the FIRST absent path; when <repo>--<slug> is absent but <repo>--<namespaced> already holds the branch, 'git worktree add' fails ('branch already used by worktree') and the '-b' retry fails (branch exists) — the existing namespaced checkout is never reached, so ensureFixerWorktree returns err and the fixer lane reports no-worktree despite a valid checkout. Repro shape: branch work/x, bro--x removed earlier, bro--work-x still on work/x. PRE-EXISTING: identical loop in commands/drive.ts before the bro-jamp7 move (verified verbatim); deferred because the extraction contract is behavior-identical — fix belongs in a follow-up: on addFixerWorktree failure continue to the next candidate and only return err after all candidates are exhausted.

issues.title: conductor: declare+implement ACP terminal capability — devin shells become bro-serve-managed, output pollable
issues.description:
Verified: devin's acp adapter implements the Zed terminal protocol —
binary strings carry terminal/create, terminal/output,
terminal/wait_for_exit, terminal/kill (plus fs/read_text_file,
fs/write_text_file). We hard-declare terminal:false in acpInit
(packages/providers/src/acp.ts:291), so devin runs shells in-process
and its terminals are invisible to anything but its own UI.

Change (conductor path only — opt-in, not global):
1. ProviderWireOpts.acp gains `terminal?: boolean`; acpInit declares
   it. client() registers handlers ONLY when enabled (the
   capability-honesty rule — acp-worker.ts:192 pattern).
2. terminal registry inside bro serve: spawn via child_process,
   ring-buffer stdout+stderr, track exit. Handlers:
     terminal/create    {command,cwd?,env?} -> {terminalId}
     terminal/output    {terminalId} -> {output, truncated}
     terminal/wait_for_exit -> {exitCode} (honor request cancellation)
     terminal/release   free buffer (kill if live)
     terminal/kill      signal only
3. Payoff: tool_call updates already carry terminal references — and
   the output buffer now lives IN serve, so expose it:
   GET /api/v1/terminals/<id>/output (+?follow SSE) — the frontend
   polls/streams a REAL shell, not a transcript line.

Notes:
- Processes become children of `bro serve` (not the devin acp child) —
  env parity check vs acpChildEnv().
- Scope to the conductor's acpOpen path; judge/acpCall stays
  terminal:false (no consumer there).
- Pairs with bro-btccj (tool activity on the wire): terminals give the
  durable pollable side; btccj's events point at terminalIds.

Acceptance: an acp turn where the agent runs `exec` produces a
terminalId visible via session updates; GET output returns live
content while running and final content+exitCode after.

issues.title: serve conductor: quota gate for acp lanes — rateGate/session budget before dv-acp spawn
issues.description:
Forensic 2026-11-13: Claude Code (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL -> bro serve) drove the dv-acp lane into the shared Devin account wall all day: 648 POST /v1/messages -> 324 acp.spawn, 297x429 + 81x529 + 54x500 responses, waves 00-14 UTC, silent since 14:10Z when serve exited. Journal: .git/bro/serve-turns.jsonl.

Root gap: spec bro-y3jvd wired providers.*.rateGate into the FLEET spawn prologue (laneGateAdmission in agent-connectors/core.ts) and explicitly scoped OUT the interactive/serve path. The serve conductor's ProviderLane has only reactive defenses: AcpLaneCooldown (arms AFTER a wall) and AcpDeadLoopGuard (churn). Nothing meters or caps spend BEFORE it happens. serve.limits.* in bro.config.local.json is also dead config — nothing reads it.

Session reuse cannot save this: conversationKey = prefix+first-turn fingerprint; Claude Code title-gen/one-shot calls each mint a new fingerprint -> new devin session/new (expensive discovery passes) -> concurrent-session pressure on the account (the actual free-model wall per learn note: per-account CONCURRENT sessions, resets :01 UTC).

Goal: the serve lane gets the same quota safety the fleet has — a proactive admission gate so bro refuses BEFORE Devin quota is spent, not after the wall.

Candidate design (to spec): consult providers.<entry>.rateGate through the SAME host-shared lane-gate ledger (fleet+serve share the account bucket — the ceiling is account-wide), charge per turn + spawnCost per session/new; plus a per-lane concurrent-session cap (sessions+pendingOpens vs configured max) mapping directly to Devin's concurrent-session wall; refusal = 429 + retry-after, journaled.

Related: bro-56o2a (rateGate dead — now stale for fleet path, still true for serve), bro-y3jvd (fleet gate spec), bro-i6811 (reactive cooldown), bro-q0v0e (spawn-churn incident), bro-2mri8 (rate-limit forensics diagnostic).

issues.title: fleet: residual hardening gaps on owner-only agent artifacts (sourcery review of superseded PR #633)
issues.description:
PR #633 (bro-l8c4f.4) was superseded by #659 — same bead, better implementation (core private-files.ts, fchmod-on-fd). Most of its 9 sourcery findings are already fixed on main by that design; these three still apply to MAIN's code, plus one documented limitation:

1. tmux spawn: failures between prepareSpawn and `tmuxRun new-session` (env-file write, runLine build, kill-session) escape without cleanup — the committed registry entry, bead claim, session-slot reservation, and the ambient env file are all left behind. Only the `res.code !== 0` path cleans up. Wrap the post-reservation section in the docker connector's catch shape: rm envFile, releaseSessionSlot, patch spawnError, rethrow. (agent-connectors.ts ~2754 onward; thread PRRT_kwDOUamqtM6vPCz1)

2. docker spawn: an operator `--user`/`-u` in agents.docker.runArgs selecting a uid that is neither the host uid nor root leaves the worker unable to traverse the 0700 agents dir or read/append the 0600 prompt/log over the mount — the agent dies with EACCES and only stderr hints why. Parse the effective --user (incl. `-u X`, `--user=X`, glued `-uX`) and refuse incompatible uids with a clear SpawnError before the run. (agent-connectors.ts ~4060; thread PRRT_kwDOUamqtM6vPCzs)

3. mkdirPrivateSync pins EVERY missing path level 0700 — when `<git-common>/bro` itself is absent it is created owner-only, locking other local users of a shared checkout out of bro/loop, bro/hooks, the mailbox and registry. Create shared ancestors with default modes and pin only the `agents` leaf (same for acp-events' archive dir). (core/private-files.ts; thread PRRT_kwDOUamqtM6vPC0v)

Known limitation (documented, no action unless win32 shared checkouts matter): POSIX modes are no-ops on Windows — the owner-only guarantee relies on the user-profile ACL, which a checkout outside the profile may not inherit (thread PRRT_kwDOUamqtM6vPC0G; spec bro-l8c4f.4 documents this).

issues.title: the merge verdict reads only GitHub PR links — a GitLab MR claim is refused
issues.description:
Found on PR #960 (bro-4cxnd): the merge step's verifier resolves PR references from the GitHub link form (/owner/repo/pull/N) and the bare #N form. A GitLab merge-request link (/owner/repo/-/merge_requests/N) names no PR, so the claim is unverifiable and the step stays open — fail closed, which is the designed behaviour, but the verdict cannot read an MR at all.

The mirror case, same root cause (CodeRabbit on packages/convoy/src/verify.ts): when the GitLab connector is selected and GH_HOST is unset, a GitHub-shaped link passes the host check — the connector is asked about PR #12 in a repository it reads as merge requests, and a MERGED answer there closes the step for a GitHub PR that never merged. The verdict needs the SELECTED connector's host, not the GitHub host from the environment.

To close it: a second review connector that answers for merge requests, a reference form the verifier recognises (the MR path), and the connector's own host in the verdict's identity checks. The parse side is the easy half; the host half is a connector.

Pointer: PR #960, the codeant-ai finding on packages/core/src/gh.ts and the CodeRabbit finding on packages/convoy/src/verify.ts.

issues.title: specs/sessions: **WARNING:** "Same per-session lifecycle as the arming markers" overstates it — the markers' lifecycle includes `armSes…
issues.description:
**WARNING:** "Same per-session lifecycle as the arming markers" overstates it — the markers' lifecycle includes `armSession`'s prune, which only sweeps the flat marker dir. The `hinted/` precedent this spec cites documents exactly this gap and closes it in code: "hinted/ sits below the dir armSession prunes, so stale markers need their own sweep" (`markSkillHinted` runs a same-TTL best-effort sweep on every write). The spec specifies no equivalent sweep for `trace/` and `fired/`, so a literal implementation of milestone .3 leaves one JSONL file per session (one line appended per post-tool event) accumulating forever in the shared `<git-common>/bro/hooks/` tree. Specify the prune — who sweeps the subdirs and on what TTL (e.g. the hinted-style same-TTL sweep on append, or a per-file size/age cap).

issues.title: react: bro react <target> <how> for PR/MR reactions (downvote on false-positive findings) + act batch optimization
issues.description:
# react: bro react <target> <how> + act batch optimization

## Motivation

When an act agent decides a review finding is a false positive (or
otherwise wants to signal agreement/disagreement on a finding), there must
be a visible, machine-recorded reaction on the host artifact — a downvote
on GitHub / a downvote (or equivalent award emoji) on GitLab. Today there
is no bro CLI surface for reactions at all, and act has no way to express
"this finding is wrong" beyond a reply + resolve. The reaction must be
applicable to both GitHub and GitLab, and it must be driven through bro
(not raw gh/glab), so the host differences stay inside the connectors.

## CLI semantics (proposed)

`bro react <target> <how>` where `<target>` is any artifact bro already
knows how to address, and `<how>` is the reaction kind.

Target forms (must all resolve):
- PR/MR ref in host-native shorthand: `#123` (GitHub), `!123` (GitLab),
  or a bare number with `--repo`/cwd context.
- Direct artifact URL: `https://github.com/o/r/pull/123`,
  `https://gitlab.com/g/p/-/merge_requests/123`, and their review/thread/
  comment deep links.
- Drill-down to a specific artifact inside a change request:
  change request (PR/MR) → review → thread → comment, each addressable
  by its unique id. E.g. `bro react thread PRRT_... -1` or
  `bro react comment 1234567890 +1`. Thread/comment ids are the host's
  unique ids (GitHub review thread node id / comment database id;
  GitLab discussion id / note id).

Reaction kinds (`<how>`):
- `+1` / `-1` (upvote/downvote) — the primary need is `-1` for false
  positives.
- Host-native emoji names where applicable (`thumbs_down`, `eyes`, …) as
  an alias layer on top of `+1`/`-1`.
- `--remove` to undo a previously applied reaction (idempotent).

Output: machine-readable (`--json`) with the artifact id, reaction, and
resulting counts; TSV for batch pipelines.

## Hierarchy / data model

bro's review host facade (`ReviewFacade` in packages/core/src/review.ts)
already models: PR/MR → review threads → comments. Reactions attach to
comments (and, on GitLab, to discussions/notes; on GitHub to issue/PR
comments and review comments). The facade needs a reaction capability
parallel to `resolveThread`/`replyThread`, with host-specific id
translation kept inside the github/gitlab connectors. Target resolution
(PR ref → thread → comment) should reuse the existing thread fetch path
so a single resolve step yields the comment id.

## Act integration

In the act loop, when a finding is judged a false positive, the agent
should apply a downvote reaction to the originating thread/comment (and
optionally reply with the reason) before resolving. This must be expressible
as a verdict action in the act plan (alongside fix/reject/defer) so it
flows through `bro review act resolve`/`reply` machinery and the ledger.

## Second topic: batch optimization of act

Act currently issues one query/mutation per thread for reactions, replies,
and thread resolutions. For PRs with many threads this fans out into a
large number of gh/glab subprocesses. Optimize by:
- Batch GraphQL mutations for GitHub: resolve multiple threads, reply to
  multiple threads, and add reactions in a single aliased mutation
  (mirroring the existing aliased-query pattern in packages/github/src/
  reviews.ts `aliasedPrQuery`/`scanMergedPrs`).
- Batch REST/GraphQL for GitLab equivalents.
- Reuse the bulk fetch paths (`reviewThreads` pagination already; add a
  bulk thread-id → comment-id map) so reactions don't re-fetch threads.
- Keep correctness independent of the batch path: per-item fallback when
  a batch fails, like `scanMergedPrs` misses falling back to per-PR
  probes.

## Acceptance

- `bro react <target> <how>` works for GitHub and GitLab targets in all
  three ref forms (shorthand, URL, drill-down id).
- Downvote reaction is applied and visible on the host for a false-positive
  finding; idempotent on re-run.
- Act can express a "downvote + resolve" verdict and applies it.
- Act's rea

Gap found 10.11: the bro.fleet plugin opens workspaces per ARMED tree only, and binds session panes to bro registry records — but worktrees worked by foreign sessions (devin TUI, run_subagent spawns, interactive opencode) carry no registry record, so their workspace can never show a session pane (only bus events + status strips), and a done tree's archive becomes unreachable once its claim closes.

Needed (spec-level):
1. Daemon projector writes session binds into fleet-status docs: {session:{id,events}} from registry agentsByTree UNION external planes (devin session locks->worktree, opencode sessions->cwd). fleet-status currently carries only worktree/workspace/title/status/led.
2. Plugin sessionEligibility binds doc sessions same as registry binds (partial: archive binds armed in #981).
3. Workspace lifecycle keyed on session record OR armed claim — a done tree's archive stays viewable ('done' is a status in the view, not workspace death).
4. 'waiting for the daemon projector' must not be the steady state for trees whose sessions are discoverable but unprojected.

issues.title: the title matcher rescans the tail for every '{{' — a malformed title pattern costs a quadratic scan
issues.description:
Found on PR #960 (bro-4cxnd), CodeRabbit on packages/convoy/src/title.ts:

A title pattern with a long run of unmatched '{{' and no '}}' makes the matcher rescan the remaining pattern for every opening pair — the walk costs O(n^2) on a hostile pattern. The pattern comes from a formula title and the title from a poured step, so the input is semi-trusted (an agent writes it) and the cost lands on a local CLI, not a trust boundary: a warning, not a bug.

Fix: parse the pattern in one pass — the walk already moves forward, so the closing delimiter's position can move with it instead of being searched again per '{{'. The walk's behaviour (which spans are literal, which are wildcards) must stay identical — the current implementation is the reference for that.

spec(serve): route names, aliases, and native (non-acp) lanes in the gateway
issues.description: The gateway's route prefix today IS the providers entry key, so an operator cannot expose an entry under a public name of their choosing. The operator's convention is <route>/<model>, where the part after the slash is the ACP agent's own model id VERBATIM (providerBare strips only the first segment; the remainder must match the agent's catalog leaf exactly). The convention the operator wants is devin-acp / opencode-acp / etc — the -acp suffix distinguishes a conductor lane from a native (non-acp) gateway provider, and it must be a CHOSEN public name (the type is already known from entry.type and the suffix drifts otherwise: kilo-cli is an acp entry, dirac/omp-minimax are acp without a suffix).\n\nThe spec covers the whole design, code lands in separate PRs: (1) serve.providers accepts a map route->entry (the string[] form keeps working); (2) lanes keyed by entry, routes keyed by public name, one ACP pool per entry even under two names; (3) native (api/cli) entries become lanes beside acp lanes in ONE listener — today a serve is either an acp conductor or a native byte proxy, never both.

The new feature branch silently carried 4+ unmerged foreign commits — a PR from it would have pulled another session's WIP into review and auto-merge could have landed it early. Fix: bro work enter should resolve the base as origin/<default> (or the repo's configured base), never HEAD of whatever branch the invoking checkout happens to sit on — or at minimum warn when the base isn't the default branch. Related: occupancy/foreign-session detection already exists for spawns; the worktree-creation path needs the same care.

issues.title: pipeline: memory at entry — stages never consult bro self learn probe (spec §learning plane)
issues.description:
## Gap (audit of bro-qjji2, 2026-11-11)

specs/bro-7d5nb.md §learning plane specifies: 'memory at entry — stages consult bro self learn probe where the signal changes behavior: route asks provider health, intake asks recurring DoR failures, verify asks known AC gaps.'

On origin/main f2e9d28 ZERO pipeline stage consults the learn store at entry: classify/route/review bind judge decide seams, intake/verify/accept bind their contract seams, capture is the WRITE side only (stages/capture.ts — the learn sweep on land, bro-7d5nb.6 shipped #916). The read side was never ticketed: bro-7d5nb closed 7/7 without it, bro-qjji2's children cover the agile contract only.

## Build

Per-stage probe seam (injected dep, default off or bound to bro self learn probe via adapter — provider/store-agnostic like the other stage seams):
- route: provider health/wall-rate lessons before class resolution
- intake: recurring DoR failure patterns before judgment
- verify: known AC gaps before evidence rows

Lessons must annotate the stage payload/journaled ctx (provenance), never silently alter verdicts — same 'signal, not gate' posture as classify's dim-answer rule unless the spec says otherwise. Decide probe cadence (per-invoke vs cached) — learn probe is a store read; hot stages may want a per-run memo.

## Acceptance

- A stage with a bound learn seam surfaces matching lessons in its journaled payload (traceable).
- No learn binding → stages behave exactly as today (seam optional).
- No direct store/fs calls inside stages — injected seams only.

## Relations

- Spec: specs/bro-7d5nb.md §learning plane (parent epic bro-7d5nb CLOSED — gap found late).
- Write side shipped: capture stage bro-7d5nb.6 (#916); exit-path sweeps bro-xkv42.3.
- Found during bro-qjji2 audit (decomposition-only pass).

issues.title: naming: plugins/ = bro CLI provider plugins, integrations/ = bro integrated into foreign tools — split plugins/<client>/bro/
issues.description: Direction-of-dependency naming: plugins/devin = devin AS a first-tier provider inside bro (agent/acp facades, @broject/devin); integrations/devin = bro's shim installed INTO devin (hooks.json + run.sh from plugins/devin/bro/). Today plugins/<client>/bro/ conflates the second sense only and reads like bro-internal components — which is why client-manifest rules keep leaking into packages/cli (opencode.ts, kilo.ts, adapter/* live in core; see bro-751ah). Rename map: plugins/{devin,claude,codex,cursor,opencode,kilo,pi,omp}/bro -> integrations/<client>/. Touchpoints: scripts/gen-plugins.ts ADAPTERS map + emit targets, .claude-plugin/plugin.json hooks pointer, marketplace manifests, doctor plugin detection, install docs, check:plugins CI. Policy to pin: integrations/ = shim+manifest owned by the foreign tool's contract; plugins/ = provider seam owned by bro's registry; core never names a client.

issues.title: Work the user wants to try stays a draft until they merge it
issues.description: An agent merged two PRs (bro #905, bro #907) and redeployed the live gateway before the user had opened the picker to check it. The repo's ownership contract already separates the modes: bro-review = 'a human merges', and the draft flag mirrors the merge target — so a change to try opens as a DRAFT with no gh pr merge --auto and no bro act wait --merge watcher, and the live runtime is not rebuilt or redeployed until the user merges or says go. Auto-merge + the act gate + redeploy are for work the user asked to ship.

issues.title: quota lane under-claims multi-start commands — a spawned command starting >1 session of its own kind holds one slot
issues.description: Found reviewing PR #1072 (kilo providerCensus thread): prepareSpawn's quota lane calls admitSessionSlot once → one claim regardless of sessionCapViews()[quotaKind].starts, while the cross-kind pass skips that kind entirely ('admitSessionSlot below covers this kind's full lane' — it claims ONE). A spawned command like 'devin a & devin b' (startsSessions=2) holds 1 slot for 2 sessions → kind cap and provider aggregate both under-count → over-admit. Same shape exists on origin/main (pre-existing, not introduced by #1072) and in loop.ts admitLaneSessions. Fix needs N claim paths per kind — reservation is currently a single string.

issues.title: Principal audit: reliability, product niche, integrations and docs/release alignment
issues.description:
# Principal architecture / product audit — BRO

Срез 2026-10-18: [674e3be8](https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/commit/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f). Инициатор: Petr. [Исследование и контекст](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ca43b7eb555044c4a71d159d45462500).

## Вывод

BRO разумно развивать как переносимый CLI-first слой детерминированной механики task → agent → PR → gate → review debt внутри уже выбранных coding agents. Не заменять CLI на MCP, не переписывать agent runtime, tracker, reviewer или graph framework. Самая перспективная ниша — maintainers/небольшие команды, использующие несколько agent clients и общий репозиторный workflow. Это продуктовая гипотеза: adoption/cost/retention данных и сравнительного benchmark пока не получено.

## Сильные стороны

- CLI + один portable plugin/skills tree + host adapters; semantic connectors, а не vendor-specific сценарии.
- Exit gate объединяет CI, unresolved threads, SAST и policy; debt сохраняет provenance замечания после merge.
- Трёхслойная конфигурация local > project > global, versioned plans с общим validation/execution pipeline.
- Реальные backends/facades уже есть: beads, GitHub tasks/reviews, GitLab reviews, Linear, Jira, Gas City, ACP и OTel. Их не следует заводить повторно как «новые интеграции».
- Persistent registry, atomic file publication и явные claims/recovery — правильное направление; конкретные race windows нуждаются в усилении.

## Слабые стороны и порядок работ

1. **Сначала trust/correctness:** lock ownership, stop truthfulness, spawn-registration crash window, claim capability, актуальность approval, private artifacts, строгая проверка mutation config, отсутствие повторного выполнения sverka при collection failure.
2. **Release/onboarding contract:** live docs показывают grouped commands, но npm latest 0.2.5 ещё имеет только flat dispatcher; setup/config filename и Node minimum тоже расходятся.
3. **Стабилизировать контракт:** тонкие CLI adapters над fleet/loop services, публичный backend extension seam, runtime plugin validation, schemas и per-client conformance. CLI остаётся главным контрактом.
4. **Затем тонкие интеграции:** SARIF → существующий debt ledger → tasks; opt-in MCP descriptors для ACP workers; GitLab Issues; унификация OTLP; Gas City ownership runbook.
5. **Доказать продуктовый эффект:** paired native-vs-BRO benchmark, progressive onboarding и измеримые lifecycle outcomes вместо обещания «ещё одной команды агентов».

## Ниша и альтернативы

Claude/Codex native automation — ближайшие частичные substitutes и одновременно execution hosts. Gas City — существующий complement/backend, OpenHands — более широкий execution-platform substitute/complement. LangGraph/CrewAI — frameworks для построения отдельного приложения, не прямые drop-in replacements. Aider — coding-plane complement; CodeRabbit — reviewer/source of findings, не цель вытеснения. Рекомендуется portable lifecycle layer; узкий review-closure entry point — вариант уменьшения onboarding. Полная orchestration platform — отдельная смена рынка, не автоматически следующий шаг.

## Документация и опубликованный сайт

Проверены HTTP-content и source, npm metadata и опубликованный tarball. Live site в целом передаёт plugin/gate/debt narrative, но актуальность неоднородна: main, npm package, generated reference и hand-written guides не привязаны к одному version boundary. Нужны release-aware examples, корректный three-layer config guide, canonical grouped reference, discoverable approval/tracker capabilities, Node >=22.18 и честная freshness/error диагностика debt showcase.

## Метод и ограничения

Пять независимых read-only исследований: architecture, reliability/security, market, integrations, docs/site; затем ручная сверка и дедупликация с удалённым Beads. Code findings — статические доказательства; crash/race последствия отделены от inference и требуют deterministic fault-injection tests. Реальные утечки или успешный bypass host protections не заявляются. UI, browser screenshots, live ag

## Principal audit 2026-10-18 — gascity-ownership

Parent audit: bro-l8c4f. Source revision: https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/commit/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f.

Scope: analysis/backlog only; implementation is NOT completed. S ≈ 0.5–1 engineer day; M ≈ 2–4; L ≈ 5–10. Rough sizing, not a commitment.

### Зафиксировать scheduler/provider ownership BRO ↔ Gas City

Kind: integration; confidence: proposal; effort: M.

**Evidence**
https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/blob/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f/packages/cli/src/agent-connectors.ts#L2549-L2580 ; https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/blob/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f/packages/cli/src/agent-connectors.ts#L3010-L3018 — gc session/shared-claim mapping и запрет отдельно resolved provider, поскольку city.toml owns provider. https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/blob/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f/packages/cli/src/agent-connectors-gascity.test.ts#L333-L369 содержит duplicate-spawn/foreign-claim/reset fixtures; не запускались. Official https://docs.gascityhall.com/getting-started/how-gas-city-works получен 2026-10-18.

**Recommendation**
Опубликовать интеграционный runbook и единственного owner для claims/spawn/retry/reconciliation/shutdown/gate. Gas City — complement, не hardcoded Gas Town и не повод строить второй scheduler.

**Acceptance**
Lifecycle diagram и ownership table включают recovery; fixture coverage подкреплена versioned real-gc conformance evidence, не только stub tests.

### Consolidation / verification note

Gas City уже является backend. Новая работа — conformance/recovery contract и documentation, не duplicate connector и не второй scheduler.

### Delivery constraints

Spec first по действующему SDD gate; сохранить grouped CLI + permanent flat compatibility aliases, один portable skills tree и existing semantic facades. No breaking redesign without owner alignment. Не считать advisory/fail-open UX security enforcement. Добавить регрессионные проверки; до claims «tests pass» выполнить exact repo CI commands. Локальные build/test/typecheck, live agents, UI и fault injection в аудите не выполнялись.

issues.description:
## Principal audit 2026-10-18 — acp-mcp

Parent audit: bro-l8c4f. Source revision: https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/commit/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f.

Scope: analysis/backlog only; implementation is NOT completed. S ≈ 0.5–1 engineer day; M ≈ 2–4; L ≈ 5–10. Rough sizing, not a commitment.

### Опционально передавать read-only MCP servers в ACP worker sessions

Kind: extension; confidence: verified: MCP list пуст; proposal: новая конфигурация; effort: M.

**Evidence**
Worker всегда делает session/new с mcpServers: []: https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/blob/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f/packages/providers/src/acp-worker.ts#L263-L285; provider/judge path также пуст: https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/blob/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f/packages/providers/src/acp.ts#L337-L347. BRO MCP уже capability-gated: https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/blob/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f/packages/mcp/src/tools.ts#L66-L82. Официальный ACP session setup поддерживает mcpServers descriptors: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-setup . MCP tools: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools .

**Recommendation**
Контракт: opt-in per-provider worker mcpServers из merged config local > project > global; начать с stdio descriptors, HTTP/SSE только по negotiated capability. Предлагать BRO read planes; judge по умолчанию оставить без tools. Не реализовывать generic mcp/message relay: ACP agent сам подключается к перечисленным servers. Польза: тот же board/fleet/tasks контекст доступен ACP agent без специальных shell prompts. Reuse: существующий BRO MCP server и ACP session contract. ### публичная debt-витрина зависит от anonymous API quota

Kind: site-reliability; confidence: verified HTTP / inferred UI impact; effort: M.

**Evidence**
[Debt page](https://broject.dev/debt/) [сначала разрешает data ref через GitHub REST](https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/blob/674e3be8ee16d703116dab218fcfaf407a96528f/site/src/routes/debt.tsx#L104-L118). При аудите этот [endpoint](https://api.github.com/repos/ThePlenkov/bro/git/ref/bro/data) возвращал 403, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`; [raw summary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ThePlenkov/bro/refs/bro/data/.agents/review-debt/debt-summary.json) отвечал 200: `generated_at=2026-10-12T09:00:50.835Z`, `open_count=70`. Код превращает отсутствие SHA в `data ref not found`, скрывая реальную причину. Общий egress/IP делает этот риск воспроизводимым для части посетителей; универсальный outage не доказан. «Live» не равно непрерывно обновляемые данные.

**Recommendation**
cacheable snapshot/fallback вне browser quota, различимые HTTP errors и явный возраст snapshot; не помещать токен в клиент. [GitHub rate-limit contract](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api).

**Acceptance**
при REST 403/429 страница показывает последний доступный snapshot или корректную rate-limit диагностику, не ложный missing-ref; timestamp/age видны и не выдают старые данные за новые.

wall speed under a token-denominated quota — hooks are small single-digit %;

issues.title: conductor: hard-denied acp client methods are load-bearing assumptions — guard or document
issues.description:
The conductor's acp client (acpOpen, packages/providers/src/acp.ts:685)
answers ONLY session/request_permission — with denyPermission — and
declares fs.readTextFile/writeTextFile:false, terminal:false in
acpInit (acp.ts:291).

Today this is safe ONLY because DEVIN_PERMISSION_MODE=dangerous on the
serve process means devin never asks. If that env/config changes to a
prompting mode, every write/exec fails with permission-denied and the
failure reads like an agent bug, not a config trap. Same shape:
elicitation/create exists in devin's binary — unused today, would hit
method-not-found if ever exercised.

Fix options (pick smallest honest): (a) conductor startup warns when
the provider env can't confirm non-prompting mode; (b) request
failures get a one-line hint naming the denied method + the env that
would have prevented it; (c) document in the conductor spec that
request_permission deny assumes non-interactive mode.

issues.title: bro debt sync runs 'bd init' inside linked worktree — fails on existing dolt server
issues.description:
Repro: run 'bro review debt collect' from a linked worktree (e.g. bro--bro-herdr). Scanning works, evidence is written, then the projection step runs 'bd init --stealth --skip-agents --skip-hooks --quiet' in the worktree cwd. bd refuses: 'Found existing Dolt database: dolt server at 127.0.0.1:37934 / This workspace is already initialized. Aborting.' — sync exits 1 with 'evidence is written; run bro debt sync to retry'.

Observed 2026-10-30, worktree /home/pepl/projects/bro--bro-herdr on shared server 37934.

Fix direction: run bd init in the common git dir (git rev-parse --git-common-dir) instead of cwd, or detect the already-initialized state and skip init (bd list succeeds fine — the server is shared). The init call needs the same resolution beads itself uses, not the process cwd.

Found during bro-l8wqu dogfood.

issues.description:
Run `bro act wait --merge --squash` from the worktree: the watcher polls the
exit gate and lands the PR the moment it settles green — in orchestration

the worktree deliberately, after the bead is closed.
If it refuses because reviewers are still pending or threads arrived after
pr-gate, keep working: fix/defer threads, then merge again. Never use
`gh pr merge` and never wait for a human — the merge is yours.

issues.title: drive rebase: second-order retarget race — base resolved before spawn can go stale again (PR #1048)
issues.description: Deferred from https://github.com/ThePlenkov/bro/pull/1048 thread PRRT_kwDOUamqtM6281UY (codeant, Major/Rarely). In the CONFLICTING→rebase-fixer leg (now packages/rig/src/policies/drive.ts ~L940, moved verbatim from packages/cli/src/commands/drive.ts L1250): after metaOf() returns after.baseRef != meta.baseRef we fetchBaseTip(after.baseRef) and spawn against it — but a SECOND retarget during that ~1s fetch leaves the fixer rebasing onto a base the PR no longer targets. The supervision loop self-corrects on the next pass (still-conflicting → retry), so the blast radius is one wasted fixer spawn, but a bounded re-probe (re-read prMeta once after the moved fetch; if baseRef moved again, return a 'retargeted' verdict and let the next pass resolve) closes it cleanly. Not fixed in the port PR: the port contract is behavior-identical and this race is pre-existing in the moved code. External ref: PRRT_kwDOUamqtM6281UY

issues.title: Interactive setup wizard — configure bro from zero
issues.description:
Product idea (operator, 2026-10-30): `bro` ships an interactive TTY wizard for a fresh operator — 'bro setup' (or first-run detection when no config exists).

Flow sketch:
1. Probe the machine for installed agent CLIs (claude, codex, opencode, devin, omp/kilo/... — detection table = PROJECT data: command names + version flags, lives in core as a provider catalog).
2. Present a provider catalog with FACTUAL entries (CLI, transport acp/cli, typical models, known limits) — knowledge level: project docs/catalog, not config.
3. Ask DEPLOYMENT questions (operator answers = personal config): which providers/lanes to enable, worker counts (fleet.maxConcurrent), class→provider routing assignments, defaults (loop.profile).
4. Write answers ONLY to the personal layer: ~/.config/bro/config.json (global) and/or bro.config.local.json (gitignored override). NEVER touch committed bro.config.json.
5. Verify: bro doctor + a dry-run spawn plan.

Acceptance: fresh machine → wizard → working loop against operator's own providers; provider catalog extensible without core changes (presets as data); respects three-layer config (AGENTS.md).

issues.title: watch pulse burns gh quota — 120s fleet sweep per rig is a rate-limit generator
issues.description:
The postTool pulse rearm (watch-pulse.ts pulseCheckpoint) is deduped correctly — but the armed `bro watch --every 120 --notify` child itself runs a full gh API fleet sweep every 120s: open-PR listing (the 'PR lookup failed — gh api failed' spam in attention is the quota dying), plus dolt reads and mailbox notify per postTool drain. Every rig with a pulse × every session = compounding gh burn. Observed live: watch output repeatedly fails its own PR lookup on gh api.

Options: event-driven pulse (wake on mailbox/act transitions instead of polling), much rarer cadence when the fleet is idle, gh-call budget in the sweep, or pulse only while a mol/PR is active. Also the learn probe found the digest reads stale planes ('no PRs' with 12 open) — cadence aside, the sweep's read-plane is blind.

issues.title: brouter: the router as its own package — the served catalog, the client layer, the acp client, ask
issues.description:
bro is the agent-workflow rig (skills, hooks, scripts). brouter is the OTHER half: the model router — the server that fronts ACP agents behind Anthropic/OpenAI dialects, the clients it configures, an acpx-like ACP client, and 'ask' (a shortcut: send a message to an ACP agent). Both live in one project; bro may become thinner.

Boundary: brouter owns the model catalog, the client adapters, and the protocol clients. bro keeps the agent workflow and delegates the routing surfaces to brouter.

Milestones: M1 the client layer (abstract ClientAdapter + claude-code pilot: the served catalog rendered into the client's own model block — the client filters its gateway discovery by /(claude|anthropic)/i, so curated rows are the only path that shows an honest <entry>/<model> id). M2 the served catalog is brouter.models (a whitelist: the models the operator declares, each with its provider). M3 the interactive setter (choose models, write the config). M4 the gateway moves into brouter; bro serve delegates to brouter serve. M5 the ACP client (acpx-like) + ask. M6 the TUI/REPL.

Non-goals now: a big-bang move of the serve conductor; the TUI.

issues.title: smart routes: the route table, the router's health store, and the decision model
issues.description:
Child of bro-olfvd.

The router's headline feature: ROUTES — a task maps to (provider, model)
through a table the operator writes and a decision model that picks the
route.

The route table is a template file: TOML, kind="route", version=1 — the
plan schema's convention (packages/act/src/plan.ts). The md beside it is
prose for the decision model, not a second config dialect.

The decision model is a JUDGE — the machinery `fleet.router` already uses
(packages/judge/src/router.ts): a typed choice over the candidate routes,
shadow → enforce, fail-open, journaled. It picks a ROUTE; the table owns
the chain and the code owns health. A model never names a provider — it
cannot see the rate limits.

Health is the router's OWN state: the router serves the models, so it
keeps the ledger — per (provider, model) the requests in the window, the
rate limit it saw (429 + resetAt), the sessions it holds. One SQLite
store (drizzle + node:sqlite, no native module) and one read-model:
{available, reason, until}.

One table, not three: `fleet.routing` (provider-first) and `brouter.models`
(model-first) become routes; the old sections are the compatibility face.

The decision model may be a model the ROUTER SERVES — proxied through
the router's own gateway, so jev, openai or anthropic can all decide.

One responsibility per package: @broject/router-store (the ledger),
@broject/router-routes (the table), @broject/judge (routePick, beside
routeClass), @broject/brouter (the CLI surfaces), @broject/cli (the spawn
path). core holds the shared contract.

Order: the store → the route table (the served catalog is its candidate
universe, epic M2) → health → the decision model → the resolver and the
spawn path.

issues.title: S1 — the router's own store: the health ledger in SQLite (drizzle + node:sqlite)
issues.description:
S1 of bro-olfvd.1 — the router's own store.

The router serves the models, so the router keeps the ledger: per
(provider, model) the requests in the window, the rate limit it saw
(429 + resetAt), the sessions it holds.

One SQLite database owned by brouter: drizzle-orm over Node's built-in
`node:sqlite` (drizzle-orm/node-sqlite) — no native module, no server.
drizzle-orm@1.0.0-rc.5 ships the node:sqlite driver/session/migrator
trio; the stable 0.45.x line does not (it has better-sqlite3/libsql) —
the RC pin is deliberate and the fallback is written down here.

The migrations are HAND-WRITTEN SQL (a list in the package) and a drift
test proves the SQL and the drizzle schema agree — every table, every
column (PRAGMA table_info against the schema). No generator, no codegen
step, no folder to ship.

Path: ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/brouter/router.db — NOT the git
common dir: brouter runs without beads, the bus, a git repo (bro-olfvd).

Tables: usage(provider, model, window_start, requests, tokens),
limits(provider, model, reset_at, source, reason),
sessions(id, provider, model, started_at, ended_at).

Every write is best-effort and never blocks a request: the store is a
ledger, not a gate — a missing or unwritable store costs the numbers,
never the run (the devin lane's precedent, packages/devin/src/usage.ts).

Surface: `brouter store` (path | migrate | stats).

Spec: specs/bro-olfvd.1.md (S1).

issues.title: S2 — the route table: the TOML route template (kind=route) and the served catalog as its universe
issues.description:
S2 of bro-olfvd.1 — the route table.

A route is a template file: TOML, `kind = "route"`, `version = 1` — the
plan schema's convention (PLAN_VERSION, `bro plan validate`, `bro run
<plan.toml>`), so the validator, the error shape and the version pin are
the ones the repo already has. The md beside a route is PROSE for the
decision model (the rubric), the way SKILL.md is prose for an agent —
never a second config dialect.

chain entries are {provider, model?} — the honest id the router already
speaks (<entry>/<model>, no protocol, no invented names). onWall reuses
the fleet's vocabulary (park | fallthrough).

The candidate universe is the served catalog: this milestone also lands
the epic's M2 (brouter.models as the whitelist) — a route may name only a
served (provider, model); naming an unserved model is a config error,
never a skipped entry.

Surface: `brouter routes list | validate`.

Spec: specs/bro-olfvd.1.md (S2).


Implemented (commit c9c2548f + the served-universe follow-up): the check
is PURE — the table and the declaration, no IO — and it lives beside the
table it judges (@broject/router-routes, unservedChains).

  - the chain names the SERVED ids the catalog speaks: devin-acp serves
    the swe-2 family, so devin-acp/swe-2-high is a model and
    devin-acp/claude-opus-5 is not;
  - a route whose chain CONTRADICTS what brouter.models declares for
    that provider is a config error, never a skipped entry: brouter
    routes validate names it, brouter route refuses, and the spawn path
    refuses to run;
  - a declaration SILENT about a provider is no verdict (absent = off):
    the rule bites only where the operator has already spoken. The
    router's own catalog still owns what an acp lane advertises.

Specs: specs/bro-olfvd.1.md (S2).

issues.title: S3 — health: the read-model over the router's store
issues.description:
S3 of bro-olfvd.1 — health.

One read-model over the router's store, computed by code — never by the
model: HealthSnapshot — key "<provider>/<model>" →
{available, reason, until?}.

Sources: the router's own ledger (usage inside the window; the wall it
saw) plus the walls observed at call time (429 → resetAt).

The fleet's planes stay bro's for now. When `bro serve` delegates to
`brouter serve` (the epic's M4), the fleet's signals can be written INTO
the same store — one read-model, two writers, each owning its rows.

Surface: `brouter health --json`.

Spec: specs/bro-olfvd.1.md (S3).

issues.title: S4 — the decision model: the judge picks the route, the code owns the chain
issues.description:
S4 of bro-olfvd.1 — the decision model.

The judge, exactly the machinery `fleet.router` already uses
(packages/judge/src/router.ts): a typed `choice` question whose options
are the CANDIDATE ROUTES (already health-filtered); each route's
criterion is its chain plus its md rubric.

Modes shadow | enforce | off: shadow journals the verdict and picks
nothing, enforce honors a confident on-criteria pick. Fail-open:
JudgeUnavailable is "no verdict", never a gate input — the caller keeps
the statically resolved route. Journal kind `route-pick`, beside
`route-class`.

The model may be a jev model served through the provider judge
(packages/judge/src/provider-judge.ts — e.g. typesafe/jev-1.13), or any
provider.

The provider may also be a model THE ROUTER SERVES (typesafe/jev-1.13,
openai/gpt-5, anthropic/…) — proxied through the router's own gateway,
so the decision model is just another model the router fronts. The wire
follows the host: a lane may speak the systemone wire (the native typed
judgment); the gateway does not (it serves /v1/chat/completions,
/v1/messages, /v1/responses, /v1/models), so a PROXIED model answers in
prose — usable in shadow, refused under enforce by the typed-grade gate.
Serving /v1/systemone is the follow-up that unlocks it.

THE MODEL PICKS A ROUTE. The chain and the health are the code's — a
model cannot see a rate limit and must never name a provider.

Spec: specs/bro-olfvd.1.md (S4).

issues.title: S5 — the resolver and the spawn path: brouter route, fleet.routing folded in
issues.description:
S5 of bro-olfvd.1 — the resolver and the spawn path.

`brouter route "<task>" [--json]` → the chosen route, the candidate set,
the health reason for every reject, the chain, the wall policy. The
"why" is the product.

The spawn path: `bro loop` / `bro fleet` ask the router for a route.
`fleet.routing` classes become routes in the same table — the old
section is the compatibility face, one table underneath. The migration
lands as an alias, never as a flag day.

One table, not three: fleet.routing (provider-first) and brouter.models
(model-first) become routes, not competitors.

Spec: specs/bro-olfvd.1.md (S5).

issues.title: S6 — the explain surface: why this agent, why this model, what the session cost
issues.description:
Child of bro-olfvd.1 (specs/bro-olfvd.1.md).

The router decides — route → chain → (provider, model) — and the decision is
silent. Three questions have no answer at the surface:

  - why THIS agent? (which lane served, and by which rule)
  - why THIS model? (who pinned it)
  - what did the session and its context COST? (tokens, requests, money)

`brouter route` explains a PLAN (a task text) and stops there. `brouter ask`
picks an agent without saying why — and never consults the route table at
all, so the table the operator wrote does not govern the router's own request
surface. The spawn path (`bro loop`) resolves a route and drops the why. And
the ledger has NO WRITER: `recordUsage`/`openSession` are API with no caller,
so "what did this cost" has no data to answer with.

The explain surface: ONE vocabulary of slices, not a ladder of levels.

  route   — the route decision: the route, the chain, the candidates, every
            reject with its reason, the entries health dropped.
  model   — the model that serves, and its PROVENANCE: who pinned it (you,
            the route, the provider entry) or that the agent reported it.
  health  — what the router knew at decision time: the walls, the sessions.
  cost    — the session's context and cost: the turn's input/output tokens
            (reported, or estimated and labelled as an estimate), the
            ledger's window counters, and the money — or an honest UNKNOWN
            when no provider reported one. Never a zero for an unknown.

One flag, two spellings: `--explain` (every slice) and `--explain=route,model`
(only those). A level flag (-v/-vv) would hide WHICH question is being
answered; the user asks questions, so the flag names them.

The ask path routes through the table when one is declared: the chain's first
ACP-capable entry serves; `--provider` still wins; with no table (or no ACP
entry in the chain) the old resolution stands — and the explanation says
WHICH rule fired. Absent = off: a repo without a route table behaves exactly
as before.

The ledger gets its writer: the ask path records the turn (provider, model,
requests, tokens) and opens/closes the session row. Best-effort — a missing
or broken ledger costs the numbers, never the run.

Where the explanation goes: stdout where the explanation IS the output
(`brouter route`), stderr where the command has another output (`brouter ask`
keeps stdout pipeable; `bro loop` keeps its run log clean), and inside the
JSON payload under `--json`.

Honest unknowns: a fact nobody knows says so and names the source
("the agent reports no cost"), because "no requests" and "could not look" are
different facts.

issues.title: bro provider install/uninstall — write/patch ~/.claude/settings.json wiring (descoped from milestone-0 spec)
issues.description:
Epic bro-om6m8 milestone-0 asked for 'a bro provider install/uninstall verb that writes/patches the claude settings profile'. Spec specs/bro-om6m8.1.md deliberately shipped a different contract instead: 'bro provider env --json' prints the settings.json block verbatim ({"env":{"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL":"http://127.0.0.1:4545"},"apiKeyHelper":"bro provider ensure"}) and the operator pastes it once into ~/.claude/settings.json. provider.ts only ever PRINTS the block (provider.ts:443,702-711) — nothing writes user config, matching the repo philosophy that tools never mutate operator settings (scripts/claude-code-live-check.ts header).

IF this convenience is still wanted, the work is:
- 'bro provider install' — read ~/.claude/settings.json (create if absent, preserve all existing keys), merge env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4545 and apiKeyHelper='bro provider ensure', write back atomically (tmp+rename), print a diff of what changed. Decide user-vs-project settings scope explicitly (user-level is the shipped contract).
- 'bro provider uninstall' — remove ONLY the keys bro wrote (match by value, never delete a user-edited value silently); --force to remove regardless.
- Edge cases: settings.json absent/malformed (refuse with the block printed instead), other env.* keys preserved, apiKeyHelper already set to something else (warn, don't clobber without --force), XDG/config-dir overrides for tests.
- Tests in provider.test.ts style + docs in site/content/docs/commands/provider.md + skills/provider/SKILL.md.

Severity rationale: P3 — the functional milestone-0 requirement (wire once, survives panes/repos, dynamic token) is fully shipped and live; this is pure convenience on top of a deliberate spec descope. Owner may also reasonably decide the manual block IS the contract and close this as wontfix.

issues.title: fleet leases phase 2: git CAS store on origin refs/bro/leases + soft interactive bead leases
issues.description:
Deferred scope from specs/fleet-routing/bro-r8y77.md 'Phase 2 (not now)' — tracking bead bro-r8y77.4 was closed as superseded but only its stash-WIP half was; these two deliverables remain unimplemented on origin/main and were left untracked. Audit bro-r8y77 2026-11-11 verified both absent: no refs/bro/leases anywhere in packages/, and 'bro work enter' (packages/cli/src/commands/work.ts) uses claimLockPath file locks + in-tree .work markers, never localLeaseStore.

SCOPE (from spec §C 'Phase 2'):
1. Git CAS lease store: LeaseStore impl persisting leases on origin ref refs/bro/leases/<encodeURIComponent(key)> using 'git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected>' CAS like refs/bro/data (see packages/core/src/dataref.ts push-with-CAS-retry pattern). Gives cross-host lease visibility — today localLeaseStore is per-host under $XDG_STATE_HOME/bro/projects/<projectId>/leases/, so two machines sharing one origin can still double-claim.
2. Soft interactive bead leases: 'bro work enter' / bd --claim hook flows acquire a soft bead/<id> lease so an interactive session and a spawned worker can't both hold the same bead. Must stay SOFT — warn/annotate, never hard-block the human's checkout; hook-flow integration lives in the work/claim path, not prepareSpawn.

Cold-implementation notes: LeaseStore interface is already the seam (packages/core/src/leases.ts acquire/renew/release/read/rebind/forceRelease/list); localLeaseStore is the reference impl. CAS store must implement the same interface so callers (agent-connectors acquireSpawnLease, holdRoleLease, skipLeasedBeads, fleet leases CLI) swap stores by project config. Watch: lease files are per-key today — a git-ref store wants one ref per key or a packed ref+index; pick per-key refs first (simpler CAS, matches spec). Token-checked release semantics must survive the round-trip.

issues.title: Gateway /v1/models latency breaks Claude's dynamic model picker
issues.description: Claude Code's gateway model discovery (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1) queries GET /v1/models on the base URL with a 3s default timeout (CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS). The conductor's /v1/models reads every lane's catalog over ACP on each call and answers in 5-10s, so discovery times out and the /model picker falls back to the static Anthropic list. Measured 2026-11-04: 3000ms -> 'gatewayDiscovery failed: timed out after 3000ms'; with the timeout raised to 20000ms -> 'cached 89 models'. Workaround in place: global ~/.claude/settings.json sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:44927, apiKeyHelper=bash /home/pepl/.config/bro/claude-apiKeyHelper.sh, CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS=20000. Fix: cache the merged lane catalog in the conductor (short TTL) so /v1/models answers in ms, and document the timeout requirement in skills/provider/SKILL.md.

issues.description:
spec.ts scaffold writes '---
parent: <id>
---' but .husky/pre-commit runs biome format on staged .md files; biome parses 'parent: x
---' as a setext H2 and rewrites it to '## parent: x' — so the specParent() frontmatter edge silently never parses for any spec committed through the hook (specs/bro-36sx7.5.md, bro-36sx7.2.md are mangled examples; the MD041 disable-comment is the current hatch). Fix: exclude specs/*.md from the pre-commit format set, or teach spec.ts to write the heading form.
