issues.title: brouter M5: the protocol clients — brouter ask (one question to an ACP agent) and brouter acp (the acpx-like stdio facade)
issues.description:
Child of bro-olfvd.

The router is a protocol thing, so it speaks the protocols: an ACP client and an LLM shortcut.

brouter ask — one question to an ACP agent, the answer printed. Reuses @broject/providers' acpConverse (initialize → session/new → set model → prompt → pump): no new protocol code.

brouter acp — the acpx-like facade: an ACP endpoint over stdio that fronts a configured ACP provider, so any ACP client (an IDE, another agent) drives the router's agent as if the router were one agent. Reuses acpOpen + acpSessionRetain (a live target session) and the SDK's agent() factory; the client's session/update notifications are relayed from the target's updates, and the target's client-bound calls (permission, fs, terminal) bridge to the real client.

The provider entries come from bro.config.json providers.<name> — the same file brouter providers prints.

Scope: packages/brouter (ask + acp), the CLI wiring, tests, the skill. Out of scope: the interactive model setter (M3), the served-catalog whitelist (M2), moving the gateway (M4).

issues.title: Define backlog auditor role and prioritization control flow
issues.description:
## Problem
В текущем процессе не хватает явной роли backlog auditor: непонятно, кто отвечает за качество и ранжирование очереди по всем источникам (beads, convoys, review-debt, .agents/backlog, уроки), и кто стратегически контролирует приоритеты при делегировании работы worker/subagent.

## Proposed action
1. Зафиксировать модель ролей и контроля приоритизации:
   - Policy owner (человек/triage-owner): задаёт и контролирует политику приоритетов (цели, веса, классы, WIP-лимиты, tie-breakers, правила override).
   - Backlog Auditor: собирает/нормализует/дедуплицирует данные из всех источников, ранжирует в рамках policy, публикует audited top-N с обоснованием и evidence, фиксирует drift/устаревшее/риски; не меняет policy единолично.
   - Orchestrator: выбирает исполнимые пункты из audited top-N и делегирует workers в рамках policy и текущих ограничений (ёмкость, зависимости, один исполнитель на задачу); не поднимает приоритеты ad hoc.
   - Worker/Subagent: исполняет, возвращает результат/доказательства/находки.
2. Определить артефакты и ритм: policy-артефакт, формат audited top-N (id/source, класс/score, why now, blockers, impact/risk, effort, evidence), эскалация override только через policy owner, feedback loop (capture/обновление очереди).
3. При необходимости привязать к существующим механизмам bro (bro status/next/review debt/fleet/convoy, bro self learn probe/capture) и описать, где auditor встраивается в цикл.

issues.title: workers leak npm mkdtemp trees in /tmp (49 x 72M node_modules) — fills tmpfs, trips loop disk-floor idle
issues.description:
## Evidence (2026-10-26 14:52-14:54Z)

Loop went `alive — idle (disk floor)` — /tmp had 705M free < 2x400M floor,
pushes held. Investigation: /tmp was 91-92% (5.4G/5.9G tmpfs) with 49
/tmp/tmp-XXXXXX dirs of ~72M each (3.4G total), every one containing
node_modules + package.json + package-lock.json — abandoned npm installs.
New dirs appeared every few minutes (15:27/15:37/15:40/15:41/15:42 local)
while the two live acp-workers were mid-task; lsof showed ZERO open fds —
all were garbage. Operator rm -rf of age>5min dirs: 49 deleted, /tmp went
92% -> 34% (3.9G free).

## Why it matters
tmpfs is RAM: the leak ALSO burns host memory (3.4G of 12G machine) —
this feeds the swap-pressure/WSL freeze class. And the disk-floor idle
halts the entire fleet lane.

## Fix directions
- acp-worker/agent teardown: scrub mkdtemp npm trees the task created
  (or point npm_config_cache / TMPDIR per-worker under the worktree).
- loop disk-floor: alarm earlier (before 2x400M on 5.9G tmpfs) + name
  the filler in the idle line.
- systemd-tmpfiles age-cleanup for /tmp/tmp-* as a safety net.

## Acceptance
- A killed-by-rate-limit worker leaves no /tmp/tmp-* behind.
- /tmp stays <50% during a 2h cap-2 run.

issues.title: conductor: verify + document pooled-peer failure domain — does devin serialize concurrent sessions?
issues.description:
The conductor warm pool multiplexes ALL sessions over ONE devin acp
child (acpOpen link reuse, acp.ts:673). Code comments assert
'concurrent sessions multiplex on the same connection' — ACP permits
it, devin's session_db is per-sessionId, but true turn parallelism is
unverified.

Two checks:
1. Concurrency probe (testkit or real): two sessions on one peer,
   prompt both, watch whether turns interleave or serialize. If
   serialized, document that parallel conversations queue.
2. Document the failure domain in the conductor spec: one child = all
   sessions die together on crash; respawn covers the next request,
   never in-flight turns; DEVIN_PERMISSION_MODE is process-wide.
   Loopback-only (127.0.0.1) is the tenancy boundary — beyond it,
   per-session isolation becomes required.

issues.title: packages/core: **🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win** **Plain notes lose their `notify` topic between publish …
issues.description:
**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Plain notes lose their `notify` topic between publish and delivery.**

`mailboxText` (Lines 52-64) writes a drop verbatim only when the event has `topic: 'notify'` and `kind: 'note'`. On the read side, `mailboxEvent` (Lines 96-99) decodes every verbatim drop as `topic: MAILBOX_TOPIC`, which is `'mailbox'`.

The result: an event that `bro notify` publishes as `notify/note` arrives as `mailbox/note`. A subscriber with `{ topics: ['notify'] }` matches nothing. Because `keep` rejects these drops, they also stay unseen until the TTL removes them. The bus connector delivers the same publish with topic `notify`. Swapping transports therefore changes what the caller sees, which breaks the facade's stated promise.

Decode verbatim text with the same topic that the write side requires.

issues.title: feat(fleet): global provider session caps — fleet.providerCaps in global config, transitive ACP lane counting
issues.description:
Global provider session caps — count lanes per provider, not per repo

Problem: the devin free-model quota locks at ~8 concurrent live sessions (safe budget ~6), and the same class of wall exists for any provider. Today's fleet cap counts registry workers in ONE repo's store — but sessions are provider lanes shared machine-wide: orchestrator sessions, watcher subagents, `devin -p` workers, `bro serve` retained acp backends, user TTY sessions, AND sessions spawned transitively (claude → devin acp) all draw from the same provider pool.

Design (feature):
- `fleet.providerCaps.<provider> = N` in the GLOBAL config layer (`~/.config/bro/config.{ts,json}`) — operator policy, not repo policy. e.g. `fleet.providerCaps.devin = 6`.
- Lane counting is global: a provider session counts wherever it was spawned — native `devin -p` workers, ACP backends retained by any `bro serve` instance, `devin acp` children spawned by OTHER providers (claude→devin still consumes a devin lane), interactive sessions. Census = registry entries with live pids + provider-pid sweep as fallback.
- Spawn path enforces the cap BEFORE spawning through the facade (`fleet agents up`, `convoy run`, `review drive`, conductor ACP acquisition): at cap → wait/park with cause `provider_cap`, never error-burn.
- Rate-limit reset waits (existing `rate_limited`+`resetAt` handling) stay the inner mechanism; the cap is the outer admission gate.

Refs: bro-r0y65 (worker-lane accounting misses retained acp), bro-zaydc (systemic spawn failure drains queue). Empirical: wall ~8 live devin sessions, budget 6 incl. orchestrator + subagent.

issues.title: acp peer: the release must kill the peer's process group, not only the child
issues.description:
The pooled peer's close path kills the spawned child (child.kill('SIGKILL')) but not the child's own descendants. The devin CLI spawns helpers; those survive the peer's death and keep the account lane busy, so the listener releases the peer's own session while the account is still consumed.

Killing a process group needs the child to BE a group leader: the child is spawned without detached, so it shares the listener's group and the group cannot be killed without killing the listener.

The fix must (a) spawn the child detached so it leads its own group, (b) kill the group (process.kill(-pid)) on close, and (c) keep the shutdown path honest: a detached child no longer receives the listener's Ctrl-C, so the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers must kill the group explicitly — otherwise the fix trades a leaked descendant for a leaked child.

issues.title: packages/cli: **WARNING:** Cron minute field wraps at 60 — intervals over an hour silently fire hourly `*/${mins}` only spans the min…
issues.description:
**WARNING:** Cron minute field wraps at 60 — intervals over an hour silently fire hourly

`*/${mins}` only spans the minute field (0–59), so any cadence above 60 minutes collapses to once per hour: `watch.intervalSec = 7200` produces `*/120 * * * *`, which matches only minute 0 of every hour (a 24h setting fires 24× more often than configured). The config bound allows intervals up to ~24.8 days, and the skill row advertises "cadence is `--every N` or `watch.intervalSec`" with no ceiling documented. Clamp `mins` to ≤ 59 with a warning, or move the step to the hour field (e.g. `0 */H * * *` when `mins % 60 === 0`) and refuse cadences cron cannot express instead of firing more often than asked.

issues.title: lifecycle: every worker session ends with learn+retro — results feed the operator session context (prompt/skills/rules) for new sessions
issues.description:
## Directive (operator, 2026-10-25)

Every WORKER session must end with `learn` + `retro`, and the captured
lessons must FEED BACK into the primary/orchestrator session context:
either the prime prompt for new sessions, or skills/rules if the finding
is durable enough to change behavior.

## Existing mechanisms to compose

- `bro self learn capture [--source drill|retro|act|mol|all]` already
  distills finished artifacts into trigger-gated lessons in the store.
- Hook session-start / prompt-submit already injects matching lessons
  (budget-capped) — the operator session ALREADY gets lesson injections
  (live example: learn-edit-write-read-relative-paths-resolve-t arrived
  as a session injection this session).
- The gap: worker session END has no enforced learn/retro step. The
  acp-worker teardown / loop exit path should run or prompt it:
  exit → (verdict?) → retro summary → `bro learn add` (if a new rule)
  or `bro learn capture` (harvest artifacts) → lessons become available
  to the NEXT session's hooks.

## Priority routing

- Durable behavior rules (paths, gates, verification) → learn store →
  injected via hooks (equivalent of prompt changes for new sessions).
- Durable but scoped (component-specific) → skills/ or rules files.
- One-off session context → watchdog/loop state files.

## Acceptance (draft)

- A worker exiting without a learn/retro artifact is flagged (or the
  teardown prompts it) — no silent exits.
- A lesson captured at worker exit is retrievable via `bro learn probe`
  from the next session and fires via its trigger terms.
- Operator primary prompt changes only through these stores (learn
  store / skills / rules), never manual prompt editing.

issues.title: auto learn-capture sweep on exit paths: loop endAudit + convoy mol done + fleet ok-exit (dedup-safe)
issues.description:
Epic bro-xkv42: lessons captured at worker exit must reach the store without waiting for a human to run `bro self learn capture`. The harvest machinery exists (`captureLessons`, sources drill|retro|act|mol) but NOTHING runs it automatically on the non-pipeline lanes.

## Where to wire (pick per lane; all dedup-safe — capture merges evidence, never double-writes)

- `endAudit` (`packages/cli/src/commands/loop.ts` ~line 4239) — after the litter sweep, run `captureLessons({sources:['mol','retro','drill','act']})` scoped to the run's beads; report `captured N lessons` in the audit lines. Fail-open: a capture error is a warning line, never an audit failure.
- Convoy/mol completion (`packages/cli/src/commands/convoy-run.ts` verdict path ~line 370-410) — on `done`, `capture --source mol --mol <id>` for the finished molecule.
- Fleet exit harvest (`ensureExitCause`/`recordedDeath`, `packages/cli/src/agent-connectors/core.ts`) — on cause 'ok' exits, cheap capture sweep; keep it OUT of the registry lock if possible (kv list is a subprocess).
- Pipeline lane is already covered: `captureStage` (`packages/pipeline/src/stages/capture.ts`, PR #916) runs the sweep on land once the run-starter lands (bro-qjji2.10) — do not duplicate there.

## Constraints

- Capture is `bd kv` + `bd list/show` subprocesses — run it detached/throttled or accept the cost; hook-path latency budgets do NOT apply (exit paths are not hook-critical).
- `--dry-run` first in tests; the sweep must be idempotent (re-running on resume merges only).
- Worker-side `learn:`/`learning:` result flags (bro-xkv42.1 contract) are the high-signal input — mol source already reads them.

issues.title: ship retro-on-stop nudge beyond repo config: built-in guard def or plugin default so every rig gets the session-end doorbell
issues.description:
Epic bro-xkv42 acceptance: "the teardown prompts it — no silent exits". The doorbell exists but only for THIS repo: `retro-on-stop` is a guard def in `bro.config.json` (~line 93) — project policy, not shipped machinery. Every other rig/repo running bro gets no session-end retro nudge.

Check `packages/guard/src/builtins.ts` + `guardSection` config merge semantics first: builtins vs config precedence, and whether a builtin can be disabled per-repo (`guard.defs` off-switch?).

issues.title: packages/cli: **🟡 Medium · Cross-dialect requests reach upstream** When the generic provider proxy is configured and a client reques…
issues.description:
**🟡 Medium · Cross-dialect requests reach upstream**

When the generic provider proxy is configured and a client requests an endpoint belonging to the other mounted dialect, `isProviderPath` accepts every `/v1/` path under either mount, and `forwardUpstream` strips the mount before forwarding, so unsupported cross-dialect requests reach the upstream instead of receiving the promised 404.

Make provider-path routing accept only endpoints supported by the mounted dialect and reject cross-dialect requests with 404.

<summary>Prompt for AI agents</summary>

Make provider-path routing accept only endpoints supported by the mounted dialect and reject cross-dialect requests with 404.

issues.description: First live transport in bro. Add a 'nats' sink type via sinks.ts registerSinkBuilder republishing bus events to subjects bro.<rig>.<plane>.<event>; config comms.backend: 'file'|'nats' + comms.nats.url (default nats://127.0.0.1:4222). issues.title: host config: ~/.config/bro providers.devin lacks type — stderr noise fails e2e suites
issues.description:
Every `bro` invocation on this host warns to stderr:
  bro.config: providers.devin type must be one of api|acp|cli — got undefined — entry dropped

Cause: ~/.config/bro/config.json has a `providers.devin` entry holding only a
rateGate (no `type`). e2e tests that spawn `bro` with ambient HOME read the real
global config and die on 'no stderr noise' assertions — ~130 help-contract
failures plus loop/wait e2e noise observed while verifying bro-ybo8z
(2026-10-27). Not fixable by silently adding a type: the entry would become a
live provider and change fleet routing. Owner decision: either give it a type
deliberately, or drop the entry / move the rateGate onto devin-acp.

Workaround for verification runs: HOME=<clean dir> npm test.

issues.title: bro review act defer — batch resolve-to-debt: file bead + resolve threads with pointer comments in one pass
issues.description:
Session mechanics repeated ~13x across PRs #815/#818: for each non-blocking review thread the fix-round-cap flow requires (1) gh api fetch of the thread body, (2) bd create with the finding text + PRRT id, (3) bro review act resolve --comment with a pointer to the bead. All three steps are mechanical and identical per thread.

Missing surface: 'bro review act defer <thread-id>[,<thread-id>...] --bead <existing>' or '--new-bead <title>' — creates/appends the debt bead with each thread's body and PRRT id, then resolves each thread with a standardized 'deferred → <bead>' comment. Also unblocks bulk deferral: 'act defer --all-minor' after the cap is hit.

The one-liner that had to be invented, per thread:
  gh api graphql -f query='{node(id:"PRRT_..."){...on PullRequestReviewThread{comments{nodes{body}}}}}'
  bd create --title '...' --type task
  bro review act resolve PRRT_... --comment 'deferred → bro-XXXX'

issues.title: act gate: count required-but-absent check contexts as blockers
issues.description: act exit_gate reported OK on PR #899 while GitHub merge_state stayed BLOCKED: the main ruleset requires 'SonarCloud Code Analysis' but the check-run never posted on the head (docs-only diff / app flake). act only counts REPORTED checks (pending/failing), not ruleset-required contexts MISSING from the rollup — so act green ≠ mergeable, and auto-merge sits armed forever. Fix: status should diff the ruleset's required_status_checks contexts against the rollup and treat absent-but-required as a blocker (or at least an alert row).
